stories.title: Judge Dismisses Trump's Defamation Lawsuit Over Epstein Letter
stories.summary: A U.S. District Judge has dismissed Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal regarding a letter he allegedly wrote to Jeffrey Epstein. The judge ruled that Trump failed to demonstrate that the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice, stating he was 'grasping at straws.' The lawsuit was dismissed with prejudice, meaning Trump cannot refile the case.

stories.title: FBI Links North Korea to $6.3 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
stories.summary: The FBI has attributed the recent $6.3 billion hack of the cryptocurrency exchange Binance to North Korea, specifically identifying a group known as TraderTraitor as responsible for the cyber attack. This incident is noted as the largest cryptocurrency theft in history. Following the breach, Binance has resumed withdrawals and reported that it has covered approximately 90% of the losses incurred by its users.

stories.title: Ciara Mageean, European Champion Runner, Dies at 34 After Cancer Battle
stories.summary: Ciara Mageean, the Irish Olympian and European 1,500m champion, has passed away at the age of 34 after a battle with cancer. Mageean, who represented Ireland in two Olympic Games, revealed her cancer diagnosis a year prior to her death. Tributes have been paid from various figures, including President Catherine Connolly.

stories.title: Halloween Weekend Gun Violence Leaves At Least 6 Dead and Dozens Injured Across U.S.
stories.summary: Over the Halloween weekend, gun violence erupted in nightlife districts across multiple U.S. cities, resulting in at least six fatalities and dozens of injuries. The most severe incident occurred in Dallas, where four people were reported deceased and 15 others injured in shootings in the Deep Ellum neighborhood, known for its vibrant nightlife.

stories.title: Violent Protests Erupt in Germany Amid Cost-of-Living Demands
stories.summary: Protests led by Gen Z activists across Germany turned violent, with significant unrest reported in cities including Frankfurt, Berlin, and Hamburg. Rioters looted shops and set fires to barricades, demanding lower living costs and improved education. The unrest coincided with similar protests in France, highlighting widespread discontent among young people in Europe.

stories.summary: The Youth Olympic Games have officially opened in Dakar, Senegal, marking the first Olympic event held on the African continent in over 130 years. The event was inaugurated by Senegal's president and features 136 local athletes, supported by 6,000 volunteers.

stories.title: Alaska Attorneys Reject Trump's Request to Set Aside Senate Ballots as 'Meritless'
stories.summary: Attorneys for Alaska have described Trump's demand to set aside Senate ballots as 'meritless' and 'not even possible.' This statement comes amid a broader investigation by the Department of Justice, which has issued subpoenas related to the case. Additionally, there is a request for a judge to separate ballots showing votes for a specific candidate until it can be determined if voters were misled into voting for a spoiler candidate.

This endorsement marks a significant shift in the race, potentially impacting El-Sayed's campaign as polls tighten in the final days before the election.

stories.title: Israeli Strikes in Gaza Result in Multiple Casualties, Including a Child
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes across the Gaza Strip have reportedly killed at least eight Palestinians, including a four-year-old child. The strikes targeted areas in Khan Younis and Gaza City, with reports indicating that five members of the Hamas-run police were among the deceased. Some sources suggest the death toll may be as high as nine.

He is accused of suppressing and manipulating an investigation into a gangland murder. Prosecutors have stated that this arrest is not connected to the recent electoral defeat of Aleksandar Vucic.

stories.summary: Bulgarians are participating in a presidential runoff election following a tightly contested first round. The vote is marked by a polarized political landscape, with candidates holding starkly different views on the Ukraine war and relations with Russia. This runoff occurs against the backdrop of recent drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and follows a record-low voter turnout in the initial round.

The situation has raised fears of the disease spreading to other African nations as new cases are being recorded.
